items.front: Alexander's father and tutor?
items.back: Father Philip II of Macedon; tutor Aristotle.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Where did Alexander defeat Darius III (331 BCE)?
items.back: Battle of Gaugamela (Arbela).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Which Taxila ruler submitted without a fight?
items.back: Ambhi (Omphis).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Whom did Alexander fight at the Hydaspes, and when?
items.back: Porus (Paurava kingdom, between Jhelum & Chenab), 326 BCE.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Modern name of the Hydaspes river?
items.back: The Jhelum.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: At which river did the army mutiny and refuse to advance?
items.back: The Beas (Hyphasis).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Which desert devastated the return march?
items.back: Gedrosia (Baluchistan).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Two cities Alexander founded on the Jhelum?
items.back: Bucephala (after his horse) & Nicaea.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Alexander's admiral who explored the Indus–Persian Gulf route?
items.back: Nearchus.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Where and when did Alexander die?
items.back: Babylon, 323 BCE, aged 32.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Which Indian ruler was his eastern contemporary?
items.back: Dhana Nanda of Magadha.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Main impact of the invasion on India?
items.back: NW satrapies, Hellenistic contact, Gandhara-art seed, path cleared for the Mauryas.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Where was Macedonia, the home of Alexander?
items.back: A kingdom north of Greece in the Balkan Peninsula.
